laws.rule: North Rhine-Westphalia's Feiertagsgesetz adds further bans on silent days. On Volkstrauertag, markets, commercial exhibitions, public sport, horse events, circuses, folk festivals, leisure parks that offer dance or acrobatics, and arcades or commercial betting are banned from 5 am to 1 pm, and musical or other entertaining performances in restaurants or side rooms with bar service, and other public entertainment including dancing, from 5 am to 6 pm (section 6(1)). On All Saints' Day and Totensonntag those same events are banned from 5 am to 6 pm (section 6(2)). On Good Friday those events are banned until 6 am the next day (wholesale markets until 3 am the next day); non-public entertaining events outside private homes and films not approved for Good Friday are also banned until 6 am the next day (section 6(3)). Public dancing is banned from 6 pm on Maundy Thursday (section 7(1)). A breach can be fined (section 11; the statute as published on this official page does not set a maximum amount). The official text read is the 23 April 1989 announcement, in force from 1 January 2000, with the footnotes shown on that page.

In a North Rhine-Westphalian forest, anyone may enter for recreation at their own risk. Cycling (not motor vehicles) and disability scooters are allowed on roads and firm paths (section 2(1) and (2)). Off the paths, dogs must be on a lead, except hunting dogs in the course of hunting and police dogs (section 2(3)). Organisers must notify the forestry authority in good time of organised events, unless the group is small and the event is for environmental education (section 2(4)). You may not enter plantations, marked closed areas, areas while timber is being cut or processed, or forestry, hunting, beekeeping or pond facilities; you may not drive in the forest (other than cycling or disability scooters on roads and firm paths), camp, or park caravans or motor vehicles, unless you have a special permission; riding is allowed only as the state nature-conservation law permits, or with a special permission (section 3(1)). Lighting or keeping a fire, using a barbecue, or storing easily flammable materials is banned in the forest or within 100 m of its edge, except at a facility the forestry authority has built or approved and marked, or if that authority grants an exemption (section 47(1); forest owners, people working there, people carrying out permitted or official measures, hunters and beekeepers during their work are excepted). Smoking in the forest is banned from 1 March to 31 October, with the same exceptions (section 47(3)). A breach can be fined up to EUR 25,000 (about A$39,727, RBA rate of 30 October 2026) (section 70(3)).

items.text: North Rhine-Westphalia's fines catalogue sets €50 to €500 (about A$79.45 to about A$795) for consuming in prohibited zones and €300 to €1,000 for consuming in the immediate presence of minors. Councils enforce. A decree says the minors ban also applies at large events such as fairs, and organisers may impose a general cannabis ban.
